---
title: Pictures
---

A DOTS PICTURE File holds a small bitmap, up to 31 rows by 255 columns, that a
TEXT File shows inline with `{picture LABEL}`.

## Draw a picture

`DotsPicture.parse` reads one line per row, one digit per pixel. The digits are the
manual's pixel codes (p. 40): `0` off, `1` red, `2` green, `3` amber, `4` dim red,
`5` dim green, `6` brown, `7` orange, and `8` yellow.

```python
from alpha_led_sign import DotsPicture

arrow = DotsPicture.parse(
    "0010\n"
    "0111\n"
    "1111\n"
    "0111\n"
    "0010"
)
arrow.height, arrow.width    # (5, 4)
```

Every row must be as wide as the first. You can also build one from rows of
`PixelColor` values: `DotsPicture(((PixelColor.RED, PixelColor.OFF), ...))`.

## Send it and show it

The picture needs a File of the same size in the Memory Configuration:

```python
from alpha_led_sign import DotsPictureFile, TextFile

sign.configure_memory([
    TextFile("A", size=64),
    DotsPictureFile("P", rows=5, columns=4),
])
sign.write_dots_picture("P", arrow)
sign.show("Go {picture P}")
```

The manual says the picture's size must match its File's entry. The library does
not keep track of the Memory Configuration, so it can't check that for you.

`DotsPictureFile` takes `colors=PictureColors.TRICOLOR` or `EIGHT_COLOR` for a
File that holds colors. On a 4120C the memory a picture costs does not depend on
its color depth (see [the memory budget](04-files-and-memory.qmd#the-memory-budget)).

Read a picture back with `sign.read_dots_picture("P")`.

## How a 4120C shows it

These were seen on a real 4120C:

- In `Position.FILL` the picture is drawn at the text cursor, in an 8-row line in
  the middle of the display, cut to its top 8 rows.
- In `Position.MIDDLE` all of its rows show, from the top row of the display.
- All eight colors light, but in three shades: dim red shows as red, dim green as
  green, and brown, orange, and yellow as amber.

## Checks

The library warns, or raises with `strict=True`, when the Sign Model has no
graphics, when the picture is larger than the model's display, and when a red-only
model is sent a pixel other than off or red.
